stem: A network performance study measures the download speed (Mbps) for a sample of 20 subscribers. The sample mean is 354.9 Mbps with a sample standard deviation of 91.7 Mbps. However, 3 of the 20 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 17 observations have a mean of 343.8 Mbps and standard deviation of 61.4 Mbps. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 354.9, 95% CI = [312.0, 397.8]. Without outliers: mean = 343.8, 95% CI = [314.0, 373.6]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [312.0, 397.8]. Point estimate: 349.4 Mbps.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [312.0, 397.8].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
